title: Recall the power reduction formula for sine squared.
text: The formula for reducing $$sin^2\left(u\right)$$ is $$sin^2\left(u\right)$$ $$=$$ (1 - cos(2u))/2. How can you apply this to $$sin^4\left(8x\right)$$?

title: Expand the squared term.
text: After applying the first reduction, you'll have a squared term. Expand it and look for another power to reduce.

title: Recall the power reduction formula for cosine squared.
text: The formula for reducing $$cos^2\left(u\right)$$ is $$cos^2\left(u\right)$$ $$=$$ (1 + cos(2u))/2. Apply this to the remaining squared cosine term.
